stages.heading: Stardate 2400.0
commentary: Welcome to yet another round of AP Bot solitiare. This time, we are experimenting with facilities. As it is our first time doing so; we will stick with just the Industrial Centers and Research Centers, facilities that were introduced in Close Encounters.

We will be increasing the complexity in other areas; taking advantage of the very many Shufflers we now have at our disposal, and also the refits made to Replay Center with the new card inventory system, originally written to facilitate resource card gameplay. We will not be playing with resources today (thus, why our stocks are at 0), but support was refitted to support other types of cards.
{cardTable}

One of the modifiers our app has dealt us is Hardy Empires, which is huge! We believe that extra starting technologies affect our starting ships right away. One card was excluded from the deck (placed into the discard pile) because it is outright incompatible with any solo or cooperative scenario.

As also shown by the table above, we will also play around with empire advantages and alien technology. Both of the choices available in our <q>hand</q> have a downside that may hamper our performance, but we decide that Fearless Race is the better of the two anyway. The AP Bot, dubbed Minotaur, will also receive one; but we do not yet know what it will be. (It will be revealed when their first fleet is revealed.)

stages.heading: Stardate 2400.3
commentary: At this point, the greatest surge of complexity is now behind us. There are still a few other areas where we will slow down, but that will be for as we progress further in this journey.

stages.heading: Stardate 2400.6
commentary: This arrangement of home systems is a bit awkward, simply because of the unique arrangement of the Massive sized versus map.

stages.heading: Stardate 2400.9
commentary: We already tow our first mineral cargo home.

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.0
commentary: And now it is economic phase time. Here is where the facility system complicates things. Our money is now divided into two types. (Up to 4 types possible depending on whether Logistic Centers and/or Temporal Centers are also used.)

Our RP is not sufficient to buy any technology yet. Probably fortunate that Hardy Empires did us a considerable favor. After paying our maintenance, we can use the CP to buy 2 more Colony Ships (-16) and 1 Scout (-6).

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.2
commentary: We finally uncover our obligatory black hole. The vulnerable scout rolled a 7, causing it to be sucked in.

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.5
commentary: Potential losses like that are one of the reasons we usually push with 4 Scouts.

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.8
commentary: ... especially since time is not exactly on our side.

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.0
commentary: Here is where things get dicey. Our oldest colony can specialize exclusively in technology if we build a Research Center, or we can add a boost to our CP prodiction by installing an Industrial Center. Since technologies get expensive fast (at least, in the earlier stages), we will choose the former for this colony (-5).
Yet, we need to take care on RP production; we can carry over a maximum of 30 RP in between economic phases. Luckily, we can spend our first 10 RP right away, on Ship Size 2 (-10).
The rest of the CP still available is then spent towards another 2 Colony Ships (-16).

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.1
commentary: We are almost done with our home systems.

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.4
commentary: Thus, no longer a reason to not step foot into deep space. Even if it means succumbing to Danger right away.

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.7
commentary: As even with the loss of 2 Scouts, we already finish our home systems off.

stages.heading: Stardate 2403.0
commentary: We take advantage of the number of colonies that had previously grown to strength 1, and built Industrial Centers on each of them (-20 total). Our CP income will hit the roof (+24 → +53 CP) by the time we are ready to spend our resources again. We also build a Ship Yard (-6) at one of the two planets bordering the warp point we just explored.

stages.heading: Stardate 2403.3 (The Trespass of Endemic)
commentary: We have uncovered our first deep space barren planet, and will be playing with deep space planet attributes. We drew Major Technology for this planet, giving them 5 non-player alien ships. The Alien-As have a tactics advantage even with our empire advantage, so they go first. They rolled 4,8,9 (1 hit ≤5), barely dispatching our offending scout.
We also run into another black hole. A 10 was rolled, sucking in our last scout.

stages.heading: Stardate 2403.6
commentary: The good news is that we have zeroed out our maintenance.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.0
commentary: It also means we can pretty much skip a turn and jump straight into the next economic phase. These Industrial Centers are far more effective than we give it credit, because it takes only a single economic phase for them to already pay for themselves.

We buy Ship Size 3 (-15) and Troops 2 (-10). We then buy a Colony Ship (-8) at our newest Ship Yard site, 4 Pipelines at our homeworld (-12), and build extra Ship Yards at each colony that already has at least one (-12). Finally, our secondnewest colony builds an Industrial Center (-5).
{prodTable}{techTable}

Minotaur begins to awaken, having placed their exploration vessels. We learned in between sessions that the first EV is given a task to explore a path to our homeworld, so it is placed accordingly. The rest are still randomly placed along their home system border. A coin was also flipped. Heads, we go first.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.2
commentary: Minotaur also uncovers a planet in deep space. This time, they drew Abundant. Since the planet was uncovered remotely, neither player knows what these NPA ships are.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.5
commentary: While the deep space colony goal of 2 is unmet, Minotaur will prioritize deep space hexes closest to their home system border.
They have found the very first pulsar throughout our adventures. This one specializes in Movement.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.8
commentary: Soon we will have a surge of actions...

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.0
commentary: But first, we should resolve our own economic phase. The sheer efficiency of Industrial Centers make it difficult to not waste CP. We buy Exploration 1 (-15), so that finishes our technology step already.

On the subject of purchases, we buy 3 Cruisers (-36) + 1 Transport (-6), filling all available Ship Yard capacity. We place 6 Space Marines at our forward Ship Yard site (-15 factoring in a freebie). We also buy extra Ship Yards at sites that already have one, and also designate F2 as a forward site (-18 total). Finally, it appears we may need a third Research Center anyway, at least temporarily, so we place one (-5) at the next eligible colony.
{prodTable}{techTable}

The most pivotal moment so far is here. Minotaur is ready to awaken the rest of their empire. Since Hardy Empires made Terraforming 1 a starting technology, they colonize their home system barren planet right away, countering the Easy difficulty <q>penalty</q> and bringing them back to the standard 9 economic rolls when playing with 20 CP homeworlds + facilities. Their rolls are 3,3,3,3,3,4,5,6,7,10.

Paranoia checks are performed for Exploration and Terraforming. 44 and 42 were rolled respectively. Both checks passed, and they buy Terraforming 2 (-25) and place a Miner (-5) in one of their nebula.
On the bid step, a 23 was rolled for paranoia. Since this check passed, no bid is placed.
Since Minotaur desires deep space colonies, it automatically launches an expansion fleet at their homeworld. It also buy Movement 2 (-20), and rolls a 1 to buy an extra level (-25).

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.1
commentary: Minotaur resumes work on exploration, but has been slowed down by a plasma storm.

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.4
commentary: Now we have Cruisers able to do the same. At least... until we uncovered a Doomsday Machine. We will engage it when we are ready. (At least, while it is not protected by a black hole.)
Minotaur uncovers another planet. This time, they draw the Builder attribute.

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.7
commentary: Minotaur takes advantage of the pulsar that their first fleet can use, giving them an extra hex the next time it is their turn for movement.
(Entry is forbidden only if fleet strategy is Hit and Run, or if they have the Horsemen of the Plains empire advantage.)

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.0
commentary: Now that our construction capacity has increased, we can use it to buy even more toys. But first, we start with Ship Yards 2 (-20).

With our increased capacity, we buy another 2 Cruisers (-24) at E3. We also buy 1 Colony Ship (-8) at F2. Our homeworld then buys 4 Cruisers (-48) and 1 Pipeline (-3). Finally, our newest colony builds an Industrial Center (-5).
Now that there are cosmic storms on the board, we proceed with rolling for movement. A 1 was rolled, prevented because home systems are off limits.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls now have to be distinguished by type, as the nebula mining giving them their first deep space roll. Anwyay, their rolls are 2,2,5,5,5,7,7,9,10 (HS) / 9 (DS).
Paranoia checks are performed for Exploration and Terraforming once more. 72 and 33 were rolled respectively. Both checks passed, and they place another Miner (-5) in their other home system nebula.
On the bid step, a 39 was rolled for paranoia. Again, the check passed, so no bid is placed.

Now that Minotaur has an expansion fleet on the board, the next launch is not automatic; but is still much more likely. A 9 was rolled, which normally does not launch. But the roll is decreased by 1 for each deep space colony the AP bot is short of the goal (in addition to being added by 1 for each fleet in service). Launch is successful anyway.

Since the Movement step is eligible, and that Movement 4 is missing, it is automatically bought. This time, we also learned that AP bots buy a maximum of one Movement level once at Movement 4+, so that ends this process.

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.3 (The Battle for Sector E4)
commentary: We consolidate 5 of our Cruisers into a single hex, where the Doomsday Machine is now exposed. Since this is not its dedicated solo scenario, we will be using its master statistics and rules for this battle. Also worth mentioning, no weakness is available for these kinds of DMs.
1. Round 1: Our 5 Cruisers have the Fearless Race advantage, so we go first. We rolled 4,7,9,9,10 (0 hits ≤2)
• The DM rolls 2,4 (2 hits ≤8)
• Round 2: The DM goes again, and rolls 1,3 (2 hits ≤8)
• Our 3 Cruisers no longer benefit from the advantage. We must overcome the corresponding disadvantage before we can consider a retreat. Thus, we rolled 3,4,8 (0 hits ≤2)
• Round 3: The DM rolls 5,7 (2 hits ≤8)
• Our 2 Cruisers rolled 1,2 (2 hits ≤2), demolishing this DM in a sudden burst of luck

Since we were successful in this battle, we get to salvage its debris right away. We rolled 1,9 on the space wreck table, giving us Ship Size 4 and Movement 2. Meanwhile, Minotaur uncovers a DM of their own, only it does not act until a combat fleet roams adjacent to it.

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.6 (The Battle for Romulus)
commentary: Minotaur is now ready to engage in its first battle against the NPA. We opt to further shake things up a bit by using the off-camera option, at least for the earliest battles (while no fleet strategy is yet known). In these kinds of battles, a single die roll determines the outcome of the battle (assuming the winning threshold is below 10).

A fleet of 90+ CP versus a 5 NPA planet has a 100% success chance (allowing to skip this roll), but will lose 30 CP worth of strength. In this case, the 105 strength fleet falls to 75, making the next battle harder to win. A colony ship is then placed on the planet (subtracting 8 CP from the budgets in the process). Finally, they take an alien technology card. We will learn it when they engage against us.

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.9
commentary: On the subject of making the next battle harder to win... it assumes no merge would take place, which is looking very likely to be false.

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.0
commentary: Now that our military is growing, our income is slowing a bit. We buy Movement 3 (-25), followed by 4 Scouts (-24) at F3, and 1 Scout (-6) at E2. Our homeworld Ship Yard capacity is then spent on Pipelines (-27 total). Finally, our forward Ship Yard sites build an extra Ship Yard (-12 total).
The plasma storm near their space rolls a 10. No storm movement takes place.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 1,2,3,4,4,8,10,10 (HS) / 1,3,10 (DS).

A paranoia check is performed for Exploration this time. An 89 was rolled. The check passed, so no technology is purchased. Terraforming paranoia check is skipped, because there are no eligible nebula to place a new Miner on (2 hexes or less away from the home systems).
On the bid step, an 83 was rolled for paranoia. Again, the check passed, so no bid is placed.
For fleet launch, a 5 was rolled, which launches easily, even despite the modifiers (-1 and +2 to rolls). The technology bank is below 60 CP this time, so the Movement step is skipped.

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.2 (The Battle for Aries)
commentary: Just before engaging against the Builder planet of Aries, Minotaur uncovers yet another planet. This one has the Poor attribute, rendering them able to afford only half as many NPA ships.

Their two oldest fleets combine (85 + 65), giving them a total of 150 CP, well beyond the threshold to be promotable to an extermination fleet. But, before it can earn this promotion, it must conduct a battle against the NPA forces. As per before, they dispatch the forces with ease, but lose some of their strength (150 → 120 CP). This combined fleet barely earns the promotion, but their Movement levels are uneven. The slowest level 3 takes precedence.

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.5
commentary: The recent promotion means that Minotaur now has a scary fleet. We do not remotely know of its composition. Additionally, they now meet the deep space colony quota; one of their exploration vessels can now open a path towards us.

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.8 (The Battle for Endemic)
commentary: We are now ready for a proper battle against the Major Technology planet of Endemic. We will screen our Transport each round (if able).
1. Round 1: Endemic's Alien-As have the tactics advantage and go first. They rolled 1,6,10 against our scouts (1 hit ≤5)
• Our fleet has the Fearless Race advantage. Our Cruisers rolled 6,3 against the Alien-D (1 hit ≤3)
• Our Scouts rolled 10,2,5,3 against the Alien-C (0 hits ≤1)
• Their Alien-C rolls a 3 against our scouts (hit ≤5)
• Round 2: Now that we no longer have the benefit of the empire advantage, Endemic's NPA ships have rolled 4,3,10,1 against our scouts (3 hits ≤5)
• Our Cruisers rolled 6,2 against the Alien-C (1 hit ≤2)
• Round 3: We are no longer able to screen our Transport. Endemic's Alien-As have rolled 1/2,9 (2 hits ≤4)
• Our Cruisers rolled 4,10 (0 hits ≤3)
• Round 4: Endemic's Alien-As have rolled 4,5,10 (1 hit ≤4)
• Our last Cruiser decides enough is enough, and retreats from this battle
<hr />

Minotaur has not had good luck exposing a path to our home systems. Luckily, their extermination fleet can safely assist in the exploration efforts, as if they had an Exploration 1 equipped ship of some kind.

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.0
commentary: Although unusually unfavorable, we did save a Cruiser, and have redesignated it as an exploration ship of our own. We also buy Fighters 1 (-25).
Using the technology we just unlocked, we buy 2 full Carriers (-54) at our homeworld, 1 full Carrier (-27) at E3. Finally, we buy an Industrial Center (-5) at H1.
The plasma storm rolls a 9, remaining stationary.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 1,1,1,3,10,10,10,10 (HS) / 1,1,9,10 (DS).
On the Exploration step, a 30 was rolled for paranoia (pass). On the bid step, an 11 was rolled for paranoia (pass).

For fleet launch, a 10 was rolled. This time, no launch takes place. Instead, a forward operating base is placed. Normally, a FOB can be placed only at a full production colony. The Builder planet they just colonized already has the infrastructure to support a FOB; so they build one there instead, and at no charge.

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.1 (The Battle for Cobol)
commentary: Minotaur uncovers 2 barren planets this turn. One of them has the Minor Technology perk. The other one has managed to pull the last Poor perk. (Aggressive / Abundant / Wealthy / Poor appear twice in the deep space planet attribute stock.)

Normally, extermination fleets would avoid NPA planets (as per scenario book). But, one of these planets happens to be in its way, and no path has already been exposed. Thus, it makes sense to use the prime directive and make it engage anyway.
Cobol's 2 defending NPA ships stand no chance at all against a size-120 fleet. The victorious fleet takes no damage overcoming this pathetic resistance.

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.4 (The Battle for Babbage)
commentary: Minotaur is now ready to engage another NPA planet. But, before it does this, it needs to make a decision with the space pirate it just uncovered. A 5 was rolled, so it hires this pirate. Since only one fleet is not in battle, it joins this fleet.

Against Babbage, this is the first off-cam battle in which the odds of victory are not 100%. A 4 was rolled, easily meeting the victory quota (of ≤7). It was not a comfortable victory though; this fleet still lost half of its strength. Since it conquered an NPA planet and has ≤60 CP worth of strength, it is now demoted to a guard fleet.

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.7
commentary: Minotaur finally exposes a path to our home systems.

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.0
commentary: But, before they can assault us in earnest, we take another economic phase break. We buy Fighters 2 (-20), followed by 3 full carriers (with 1 of them at our forward site), for a total of 81 CP.
The plasma storms have rolled 6,3 (in reading order). The storm at L7 tries to go out of bounds, but can not. The storm at I9 moves to H10.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 2,3,3,4,5,9,10 (HS) / 1,1,4,4,5,6 (DS).
On the Exploration step, a 76 was rolled for paranoia (pass). On the bid step, an 8 was rolled for paranoia (pass).

For fleet launch, a 6 was rolled. They successfully launch a fresh fleet. Since launch was successful, and they got plenty of tech money, they rolled a 3 on the Movement step (buy Lv5). One last paranoia check of 98 and they place their newest fleet at their sole FOB. Since they had 122 CP stockpiled in the fleet bank, this fleet becomes an extermination fleet.

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.3
commentary: Soon it will be Minotaur's time to assault. But, because we still have the initiative; we get to reinforce the homeworld one last time before that heppens...

Between two hexes, the nebula could be considered detremental. A 51 was rolled for paranoia. A pass, which allows the fleet to enter. While it is possible Minotaur could have chosen to assault an intermediate planet anyway, the use of transports may weaken the fleet just enough to complicate a battle at the homeworld.

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.6 (The Battle for Terra)
commentary: The time for Minotaur's assault has come. A hidden fleet worth 120 CP, coupled with a space pirate, 4 unknown alien technology cards and an unknown empire advantage... versus a Fearless Race comprising of 4 Cruisers + 6 Carriers + 18 Fighters + 6 Ship Yards (240 CP total).
Before Minotaur can choose a fleet strategy, its cards all need to be revealed; as shown in card inventory, with the empire advantage listed first.
{cardTable}

Since Minotaur has multiple alien technologies, it should choose a fleet strategy that makes use of at least one of these cards. An 84 was rolled, giving it the Scout Rush strategy and benefiting from Soylent Purple. Points are then spent as follows:
1. Fighters are detected, so it buys Point-Defense 1 (69 → 49 tech CP)
• Point-Defense 2 is also bought (49 → 29 tech CP)
• Movement is skipped (Lv4+ already known)
• On the upgrade step, a 9 was rolled (skip)
• Attack 1 (49 → 29 tech CP)
• Movement is skipped again (Lv4+ already known)
• On the upgrade step, a 2 was rolled
• Defense 1 was bought this way (29 → 9 tech CP)
• 20x Scouts (120 → 0 assigned CP)

Normally an AP bot would consider Transports when assaulting a planet. But; even if it was possible for them to screen one or more transports, they are assaulting a homeworld. Even 20 militia is a tall order for invading transports to overcome, and there is always the risk of a partial bombardment backfiring. Thus, Minotaur does not consider it a viable strategy for this battle.
1. Round 1: Even with their Scout Rush, we have more ships than they do. We will screen our Ship Yards each round (if able)
• Our forces benefit from Fearless Race this round, so we all get to shoot first! Thus, we will instead organize our rolls by final Attack strength
• We have 9 Fighters at Attack 6, so we start with these craft. Prioritizing their pirate, we rolled 1/2,4,5,5,6,8,8,9 (5 hits ≤6/5)
• We also have 9 Fighters at Attack 5, so these craft are next. We rolled 1,2,2,5,6,6,9,9,10 (3 hits ≤4)
• Our 4 Cruisers rolled 1,1,4,10 (2 hits ≤3)
• Our 6 Carriers rolled 1,7,7,8,8,9 (1 hit ≤2)
• Their 10 Scouts rolled 5,9,4,5,10,10,6,5,7,9 against our older B5 fighters (6 hits ≤8)
• Round 2: We no longer benefit from Fearless Race, and Hive Mind has started to increase their Defense; but we now gain Fleet Size Bonus (22 : 10)
• Their 10 Scouts can go again, but must conduct a morale check (11 ships were lost in battle so far). They rolled a 37 (failure ≤91), and retreat from this battle

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.9 (The Battle for Terra... again!)
commentary: Despite how victorious we were, making a sweeping advance with Tactics 0 probably is not advisable, especially since the retreat hex is also a nebula. We should make this our next technology when we have more RP.

Posture checks would have no effect on any of Minotaur's existing fleets, so we skip the corresponding paranoia check. Since this fleet of 10 Scouts is already known, they circle right around, and go straight into battle. An incoming extermination fleet also arrives, taking advantage of the fact that we have an undefended planet right next door (which does not stop movement). 122 CP worth of unidentified ships is good for 20 more Scouts.
1. Round 1: We are no longer able to screen our Ship Yards this time (28 : 30)
• Our forces benefit from Fearless Race once more. Our 12 Fighters rolled 1,1,3,4,4,6,7,7,8/5,6,10 (5 hits ≤5/4)
• Our 4 Cruisers rolled 1,6,8,9 (1 hit ≤3)
• Our 6 Carriers + 6 Ship Yards rolled 1,2,3,4,4,7,7,8,9,9,9,9 (2 hits ≤2)
• Their 22 Scouts rolled 3,9,3,5/8,6,8,3,4,3,6,9,8,2,10,2,7,1 against our fighters (12 hits ≤8/7)
• 4 Scouts still have ammo, and rolled 4,5,5,5 against our ship yards (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 2: We no longer benefit from Fearless Race, our numbers have worsened a bit (15 : 22), and Hive Mind increases their Defense again
• But, since their scouts no longer have fighters to shoot down, they have lost their PD bonus
• Thus, our forces roll once more. Our Cruisers rolled 1,2,6,8 (2 hits ≤2)
• Our 5 Ship Yards + 6 Carriers rolled 1,3,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,9,10 (1 hit ≤1)
• Once again, their remaining 19 Scouts have taken significant losses (8 lost at start of round). They rolled a 63 (failure ≤91), causing them to retreat once more

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.0
commentary: We have successfully defended the homeworld against 2 consecutive battles. We are able to do a <q>double</q> with what was originally planned; we buy Tactics 1 (-15) and Attack 1 (-20) together. We buy 15 Scouts (-90), placing them as close to the homeworld as possible.
The plasma storms have rolled 9,10 (in reading order). Neither cosmic storm moves this time.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 2,4,4,6,6,6,7,7,8 (HS) / 2,2,4,5,9,10 (DS).

Incidentally, the Poor and Abundant attributes work differently for an AP Bot than they do for human players; to the point where we integrated extra information for these (and related) deep space planet attributes. Adding them together, Minotaur would get an extra roll each fifth economic phase that is not also each tenth phase. (EP 5 / 15 / to name a few).

Now that Minotaur has suffered its first defeats against us, its paranoia has risen considerably. On the Exploration step, an 18 was rolled for paranoia (fail). This causes Minotaur to buy Exploration 2 (-15).

Their extermination fleet (of 19 scouts) is threatened, so they place a bid as if the corresponding check had failed. 2,9 were rolled. Take the lowest, subtract 3, and add the paranoia <q>tier</q> (+5), and they place a bid of 4. This causes them to take the initiative.
For fleet launch, a 10 was rolled. Once again, no launch takes place. They have one eligible deep space colony to place a new FOB, so one is built there (-20).

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.2A (The Battle for Terra)
commentary: The Scout Rush had effective synergy with Point-Defense technology back when we had Fighters. But now that the latter are no longer in the equation, it puts a decent dent in the former's viability.

Thanks to a Regional Map, they uncover another pirate. Since the previous pirate was destroyed, they rolled a 3 to hire this replacement. No eligible fleets are available (it will not merge with a fleet about to battle), so it instead goes to the nearest colony.

And since Ship Yard capacity suddenly became a bottleneck (especially since we lost 1 in the previous battle), we instead went for Scouts of our own. We trade some of our Attack potential for denying them a PD advantage.
1. Round 1: Our forces have the Tactics advantage even if we did not have the Fearless Race advantage.
• At 22 : 19 ships, we can screen a limited subset of our Ship Yards this round (leaving 2 exposed due to lack of numbers). The rest of our forces go first
• Our Attack 4 craft (4 Cruisers + 7 Scouts + 2 Ship Yards) rolled 1,1,1,3,4,4,5,6,7,9,9,9,10 (4 hits ≤3)
• We also have 6 Carriers. We rolled 3,3,4,6,7,8 (0 hits ≤2)
• Their 15 Scouts rolled 9,9,5,9,1,6,10,4/7,4,7,9,3,2,7 (5 hits ≤4), knocking out 2 more ship yards and 3 scouts
• Round 2: At 17 : 15, we are still able to partially screen our Ship Yards. 1 is exposed this round
• Our Attack 4 craft (4 Cruisers + 4 Scouts + 1 Ship Yard) rolled 2,3,4,6,6,7,8,9,10 (2 hits ≤3)
• Our 6 Carriers rolled 2,2,3,4,10,10 (2 hits ≤2)
• Their 11 Scouts rolled a 57 for morale (failure ≤74), causing them to retreat once more

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.2P (The Battle for Sector B4)
commentary: Now that a limited subset of our defensive fleet has Tactics 1, we make a sweeping advance into the nebula, sans one carrier that we instead move to the adjacent planet.
1. Round 1: Thanks to nebulaic interference, our Fearless Race's advantage is negated; but so is their Defense equipment
• Our Scouts still have the Tactics advantage, so they go first. We rolled 4,4,5,7 (2 hits ≤4)
• Their 9 Scouts rolled 3,2,6,2,10,1/7,7,8 (4 hits ≤4), knocking our the last of our scouts
• The rest of our forces rolled 2,5,8,9/2,4,5,8,10 (2 hits ≤4/3)
• Round 2: Minotaur has lost another 4 ships. They rolled an 18 for morale (failure ≤74), causing another retreat

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.5 (The Battle for Sector B3)
commentary: Their remaining 7 Scouts are numerous enough still to avoid the shattered fleet threshold. They also manage to bring the recently hired pirate over, too. Still, by positioning one of our carriers as such, it prevents them from being able to immediately just assault an exposed homeworld. Minotaur uncovers a Spaceport planet, making it one of the few times where the planet can neither be colonized, nor is it hostile in any way.
During our turn, we take advantage of their postiion, and seal off all potential retreat hexes.
1. Round 1: We benefit from Fearless Race once more
• Our forces rolled 1/5,7,9/1,3,6,9,10 (2 hits ≤4/3/2)
• Their 8 Scouts rolled 9,7,1,4,9,10,2,3 (4 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Our Fearless Race's bonus wore off, and that they now gain Defense +1; but our Cruisers still go first. We rolled 2,4,9,10 (1 hit ≤2)
• Their 7 Scouts rolled 3/1,2,6,6,7,10 (3 hits ≤4/3)
• Round 3: Our Cruisers rolled 1,2,6 (2 hits ≤3)
• Their 5 Scouts gained fleet size bonus, and rolled 2,5,6,8,9 (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 4: Our Cruisers are eligible to retreat now, but we will remain. We rolled 5,7,10 (0 hits ≤2)
• Their 5 Scouts lost the fleet size bonus, but gain Attack +1 from Hive Mind; and rolled 2,3,3,8,9 (3 hits ≤4)
• Round 5: Our last Cruiser decides enough is enough, and retreats to C3 to protect the pipeline

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.8
commentary: Before Minotaur finalizes its decisions, its guard fleet now has a cruiser near their colony. Since their shattered fleet is technically threatened, a 67 was rolled for posture. Since this paranoia check failed (≤74), the former fleet keeps defense posture, and remains still.
The Battle for Sector B4
Their fleet is now down to just 5 Scouts, which is now below the shattered fleet threshold. The safest path involves entering a nebula, so that is their choice.
After our carrier rolls a 3 (hit), they rolled 1,2,6,7,7 (2 hits ≤4), eliminating our straggler.
The Battle for Endemic
Since the only ships of ours near their 4 scouts is a single Cruiser, we opt to not pursue it any further. Instead, we have a rematch with Endemic's 3 Alien-As.
1. Round 1: Fearless Race's bonus is meaningless when their Alien-As have the best natural weapon class and also Tactics 1.
• Their 3 Alien-As rolled 1,4,9 (2 hits ≤5)
• Our 6 Scouts benefit from fleet size bonus, and rolled 3,4,5,5,7,10 (2 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Their Alien-As rolled 5,8 (1 hit ≤5)
• Our 5 Scouts rolled 1,3,7,9,10 (2 hits ≤4)
• Round 3: Their last Alien-A rolled a 10 (≤5 to hit)
• Our 5 Scouts rolled 4,6,7,8,10 (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 4: Their Alien-A rolled a 5 (hit ≤5)
• Our 4 Scouts rolled 3,6,9,10 (1 hit ≤4), finishing off the last defender and subduing the planet

stages.heading: Stardate 2411.0
commentary: We sent their last known extermination fleet running home, but at the expense of having endured heavy battle losses ourself.

Since our Ship Yard capacity was wrecked, we counter it by buying Ship Yards 3 (-25). We then buy 6 Scouts (-36) at the homeworld, 7 Scouts (-42) at Andromeda (E3), and 1 Colony Ship (-8) + 1 Pipeline (-3) at Odyssey (F2).
The plasma storms have rolled 1,5 (in reading order). The former tries to move to a hex off the map, so it instead stays. The latter moves west.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 1,2,3,6,8,8,8,9,10 (HS) / 1,1,2,5,6,7 (DS).
Their shattered fleet (of 4 scouts) is threatened, so they place another bid. 6,8 were rolled, and a net paranoia modifier of +4 causes them to place a bid of 10.

For fleet launch, a 7 was rolled. Launch was successful this time, and they can roll for Movement also. A 5 was rolled, causing them to buy Movement 6 (-20). The high paranoia means that their placement is wildly unpredictable. An 86 was rolled, which succeeds anyway. Since this is an extermination fleet, the FOB closest to our homeworld is used.

stages.heading: Stardate 2411.1 (The Battle for Sector I2)
commentary: We have a feeling this could be the beginning of the end. We shattered the previous newest fleet, only for there to be a replacement extermination fleet.

During Minotaur's turn, they unveiled another warp point with the same ID as the one adjacent to it. The AGT rulebook says to remove the one that was last revealed, so that will be done once we get to the next stage.
During our turn, we hit up the space station closest to the NPA planet we subdued last phase.
1. Round 1: Unlike the NPA ships defending their planet, space stations have Tactics 0. We use our Fearless Race to our advantage for this round
• Our 4 Scouts also benefit from FSB, and rolled 3,7,7,8 (1 hit ≤3)
• The space station rolls a 5 (hit ≤6)
• Round 2: We no longer benefit from Fearless Race, so the space station shoots again. It rolls a 9 (≤6 to hit)
• Our 3 Scouts rolled 7,7,8 (0 hits ≤3)
• Round 3: The space station rolls a 10 (≤6 to hit)
• Our 3 Scouts rolled 2,2,8 (2 hits ≤3), finishing this space station off
Since we conquered this space station, we can choose to salvage one of two alien technology cards. Bioweapons looks tempting to grab, since it synergizes well with Advanced Destroyers.

stages.heading: Stardate 2411.4
commentary: The two AP bot fleets (24 + 128 CP) have merged together (= 152 CP), causing the new fleet to be that much stronger... at the expense of having their Movement equipment knocked back down to level 3.

At this point, there is no reason to not colonize the planet we recently subdued. We do so, and get to draw 3 alien technology cards, shown in our hand. Major Technology allows us to keep 2 of these cards. Phased Warp Coil and Superhighway work exceptionally well with our play style and technologies unlocked, so we choose them.

stages.heading: Stardate 2411.7 (The Battle for Terra)
commentary: Here we go again. The combined fleet of 152 CP has made it to our homeworld once more. Before any decisions are made, an 81 is rolled for fleet strategy (keep >62). The points are then spent as follows:
1. Rolled a 3 from the space wreck that was previously set aside (Attack 2 granted)
• Ship Size 2 (44 → 34 tech CP)
• Ship Size 3 (34 → 19 CP)
• 25x Scouts (152 → 2 assigned CP)
The acid question becomes: Can we cause these scouts to retreat?
1. Round 1: All of our forces have the Tactics and/or Weapon Class advantage, so we go first
• All of our forces happen to have Attack 4. Together, we rolled 1,1,2,2,3,4,4,4,4,7,7,7,7,8,9,9,10 (5 hits ≤3)
• Their 20 Scouts rolled 7,1,5,8,1,7,1 against our ship yards (3 hits ≤4), followed by 9,8,8,10,6,7,2,4,5,9,5,7,9 against our scouts (2 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Hive Mind now gives them Defense +1
• Our forces rolled 1,1,2,2,3,6,7,7,7,8,10,10 (4 hits ≤2)

• They lost 5 Scouts at the start of the round. Even with Hive Mind giving them one benefit, the morale threshold is still extremely high (91). A 55 was rolled, causing them to retreat into the nebula

stages.heading: Stardate 2412.0
commentary: Our homeworld Ship Yard capacity is gone. Fortunately, we got two forward Ship Yard sites still able to produce ships.

Since our technology is maturing, we replace one of our Research Centers with an Industrial Center (-5). During this transition period, the colony benefits from no facility, but still produces 5 natural CP. This natural production pays for the new facility.
We buy 8 Scouts (-48) at Andromeda (E3), 4 Destroyers (-36) at Odyssey (F2), and a Defense Satellite Network (-6) at our homeworld.
The plasma storms have rolled 1,7 (in reading order). The former is demonstrating insanity, while the latter simply makes no attempt to move.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 1,3,4,5,5,6,9,9 (HS) / 1,2,3,5,6,8,9 (DS).
Their extermination fleet (of 16 scouts) is threatened, so they place yet another bid. 6,7 were rolled, and a net paranoia modifier of +6 causes them to place a bid of 12.

For fleet launch, an 8 was rolled. Normally this would be a successful launch, but a maintenance penalty of +1 pushes them into the no launch zone. Random Factor decided that Cobol (D7) would get the next FOB.

stages.heading: Stardate 2412.3
commentary: The Battle for Terra
Since posture checks are meaningless still, Minotaur's extermination fleet simply circles around and re-assaults our homeworld.
1. Round 1: We have the same advantages as last time, only that we also have satellites to help us out
• Their 11 Scouts rolled 2,2,2,3,4,5,5,6,7,8,9 against our own (5 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Our forces rolled 6/2,2,2,3,4,8,10 (3 hits ≤3/2)
• Once again, losses are devastating enough that they overcome even Minotaur's Hive Mind bonus. A 23 was rolled, causing them to retreat again
The Battle for Sector J6
We find another space station. This one is not as heavily equipped, so this next battle should be easier.
1. Round 1: Since we benefit from Tactics+Fearless Race together, we rolled 9,10,10 (0 hits ≤4)
• The space station rolls a 2 (hit ≤5)
• Round 2: The station goes again, with a 3 (also a hit)
• Our last Scout rolls an 8 (≤4 to hit)
• Round 3: The station goes again, with a 10 (miss)
• Our Scout no longer benefits from FSB, and rolls another 8 (≤3 to hit)
• Round 4: The station goes again, with another 10 (miss)
• Our Scout finally is able to retreat, and we do just that

stages.heading: Stardate 2412.6 (The Battle for Terra... again)
commentary: Their fleet of 8 Scouts still is not shattered, so they circle around yet again...
1. Round 1: Our forces rolled 9/2,3,5,7,7,8,9 (2 hits ≤4/3)
• Their 6 Scouts rolled 3,4,5,5,9,10 against our own (2 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Our forces rolled 6/1,4,6,9,10 (1 hit ≤3/2)
• Although not as devastating as the previous battle, they still must conduct a morale check. A 10 was rolled (failure ≤26), causing yet another retreat

During our turn, we send in our <q>counter</q> fleet to the pulsar near Cobol (at E5). We also encounter a pirate of our own. Considering how squishy pirates tend to be, we fight it with our lone Scout. We rolled a 2 with out Scout... easily demolishing it (≤4 to hit)

stages.heading: Stardate 2412.9
commentary: The Battle for Terra... yet again
Their fleet is now down to 5 Scouts, barely avoiding the shattered fleet threshold. They circle right around once more.
1. Round 1: Our forces rolled 7/1,2,4,7,9 (2 hits ≤4/3)
• Their Scouts rolled 1,7,9 against our own (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 2: Our forces rolled 3/4,5,6,9 (1 hit ≤3/2)
• Their 2 Scouts rolled a 29 for morale (pass >26), allowing them to stay. They rolled 2,3 against our scouts (2 hits ≤4)
• Round 3: Our forces rolled 6/1,3 (1 hit ≤3/2)
• Their last Scout rolled an 88 for morale (pass >74), allowing it to stay again. It rolled a 2 against our scouts (hit ≤4)
• Round 4: Our forces gain FSB now, and rolled 10/2 (1 hit ≤4/3), eliminating the last straggler
The Battle for Cobol
During our turn, our Defense-charged fleet of Destroyers+Scouts now reaches their planet of Cobol. An FOB is present here though.
1. Round 1: We screen our Destroyers each round, if able...
• Our Scouts benefit from Fearless Race and FSB, so we go first. Focusing on their satellites first, we rolled 4,5,3/5,10,3,6,1 (4 hits ≤4/3)
• Their Base rolls an 8 (hit ≤8)
• Round 2: We no longer benefit from Fearless Race, so the Base goes again. It rolls a 9 (≤8 to hit)
• Our Scouts rolled 1,3,4,4,6,7,10 (2 hits ≤3), finishing the Base off and leaving Cobol exposed

• Bombardment Round: Our Destroyers are equipped with Bioweapons, allowing them to bombard (and eventually glass) the colony without fail (including rendering any ground units they may build meaningless)
After the battle is over, our northern Scout exposes a black hole unassisted. A 9 was rolled, sucking it in.

stages.heading: Stardate 2413.0
commentary: Finally, our first offensive victory against Minotaur. This slows their economy a bit.
Since we finally started developing our first deep space colony, we build another Industrial Center (-5) there. We also got enough RP to buy another tech. Attack 2 is our next choice (-30).

We take advantage of our Phased Warp Coil, and use it to buy 6 Battlecruisers (-72), using all available Ship Yard capacity. We also add extra Ship Yards at existing sites while at it (-12), plus one at the newest colony (-6).
The plasma storms have rolled 7,7 (in reading order). No storm movement still...
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 1,1,1,2,3,4,4,7,8 (HS) / 3,3,5,7,7,10 (DS).
No assets are threatened this time. Still, a 13 is rolled for paranoia (fail), so they bid anyway. 3,9 were rolled, and a net paranoia modifier of +7 causes them to place a bid of 6.

For fleet launch, a 1 was rolled. This automatically causes a launch. On the Movement step, a 4 was rolled (buy for 20). One last paranoia roll of 50 causes them to place their fleet at the homeworld.

stages.heading: Stardate 2413.2
commentary: Now that Minotaur has placed an extermination fleet at the homeworld, things have become a lot more spicier now that a shell game is possible.

It appears that 3-5 different routes are fair game. Minotaur rolls to determine how many <q>copies</q> to create... of which it appears there should be 5. This process requires 4 decoys, slightly weakening the local fleet's strength (148 → 144 CP).

An opportunity presents itself where the oldest guard fleet can merge with one or more of these copies, so it does just that. The main fleet strength has increased (144 → 174 CP), but is also slowed down (Movement 7 → 4).

stages.heading: Stardate 2413.5
commentary: An opportunity presents itself to unveil 2 of these fleets. One of our Cruisers was previously assigned to guard the space wreck, and is now unveiling those fleets. A 1 was rolled, causing one of those fleets to be the real deal; ending this shell game.
The Battle for Sector I7

Now that the jig is up, Minotaur rolls a 50 on the fleet strategy step. This one failed (≤91), so it rolls a 31 for a new strategy: Fighters. This new strategy puts Afterburners to good use, at least. The fleet is then built as follows:
1. Against a known fleet and <60 tech CP available, so counter techs are skipped
• Fighter 1 (44 → 19 tech CP)
• The next sensible step is Fighter 2, which is barely out of reach
• 6x Carriers + 18x Fighters (174 → 12 assigned CP)
• 1x Cruiser (12 → 0 assigned CP)
After our Cruiser rolls a 4 (barely misses), their Fighters rolled 1,3,etc, and easily mop up our lone cruiser.
The Battle for Aries
We gained some much useful information learning what the new strategy is. It may take some time to acquire the RP necessary to counter it, but not all hope is lost.
In the mean time, we got another planet to assault. The FOB unveils another Base+Satellites combo. We keep our Destroyers screened.
1. Round 1: Our Scouts benefit from Fearless Race and FSB once more, so we go first. Focusing on their satellites first, we rolled 9,10,2,9,6,2/3 (3 hits ≤4/3)
• Their Base rolls a 7 (hit ≤9)
• Round 2: We no longer benefit from Fearless Race, so the Base goes again. It rolls a 10 (≤9 to hit)
• Our Scouts rolled 3,6,8,8,9,9 (1 hit ≤3)
• Round 3: The Base rolls another 7 (hit ≤9)
• Our Scouts rolled 6,6,7,7,8 (0 hits ≤3)
• Round 4: The Base rolls another 6 (hit ≤9)
• Our Scouts rolled 2,3,7,9 (2 hits ≤3), finally finishing the base off
• Bombardment Round: Our Bioweapons also glass this colony without fail

stages.heading: Stardate 2413.8
commentary: While Minotaur brings its newest fleet closer to our homeworld, we prepare to raid their home system colonies.

stages.heading: Stardate 2414.0
commentary: Another offensive victory for us further weakens their economy. Still, it appears the facility swap backfired on us when it caused us to be unable to afford Point-Defense.
We may have to fight their fire with our own. Andromeda (E3) builds 2 Carriers (-24) + 7 Fighters (-35). Odyssey builds 2 Carriers (-24) + 4 Fighters (-20).
The plasma storms have rolled 2,7 (in reading order). The northern plasma storm moves east.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Minotaur's economic rolls are 7,7,8,8,8,8,9,9 (HS) / 2,4,5,7 (DS).
Their home systems are threatened, so they place a bid. 6,8 were rolled, and a net paranoia modifier of +1 causes them to place a bid of 7.

For fleet launch, a 6 was rolled. Even with a +1 penalty, launch is still decently successful. They also have maxed out Movement, so no further rolls need to be made here. Since we have ships adjacent to their home systems, placement is limited to their homeworld.

stages.heading: Stardate 2414.1
commentary: Threatened home systems causes their newest fleet to assume defense posture, as they chase down our ships.
During our turn, we invade one of their home system colonies. This potentially causes random encounters. An 8 was rolled, so none appear. We use our Bioweapons to instantly destroy this colony.

stages.heading: Stardate 2414.4
commentary: They almost manage to reach our Bioweapons fleet, but is also one of the few times where having the initiative bites them: We split off one of our Scouts, and have them go around their fleet and blockade a colony behind them.

On the random encounter step, another 8 was rolled (none found). Thus, we use our Destroyers to instantly glass another colony. As for the one colony that we are simply blockading, a 6 was rolled, giving them 2 Light Infantry.

stages.heading: Stardate 2414.7
commentary: Defense Posture priorities say to favor ships closest to the homeworld, which was one of the reasons why we split one of those Scouts off. It distracts their defensive fleet and keeps them away from our Bioweapons. On the random encounter step, a 1 was rolled (none found).
The Battle for Essen
To that end, it is perfectly possible for them to change their fleet strategy, which would spoil one of our plans. A 30 was rolled, which fails this paranoia check.

A 95 was rolled for a new strategy, which gives them Yarr. This does not synergize well with their alien technologies, so we treat this as if it was a strategy they recently used. A 5 was rolled, which causes a reroll. A 32 was then rolled (for Fighters), which is the very same strategy they are currently using. A 1 was then rolled, allowing them to keep this strategy. The paranoia is still reset. Points are then spent as follows:
1. Fighter 2 (46 → 26 tech CP)
• On the upgrade step, a 3 was rolled (cannot afford Defense 2)
• Fighter 3 (26 → 1 tech CP)
• The next sensible step is Ship Size 4, which is well out of reach
• 2x Carriers + 6x Fighters (60 → 6 assigned CP)
• 1x Scout (6 → 0 assigned CP)
After our Scout rolls a 3 (hits their scout ≤3), their Fighters rolled 3,7,8,4,1,4 (6 hits), pulverizing our distraction.
The Bombardment of Vortigern

Even despite the fiasco, we still protect our Bioweapons. After 6,8 was rolled (in reading order) to add 2 Light Infantry to each of 2 colonies that are being lightly beseiged; We use our Destroyers to glass a third home system colony!

stages.heading: Stardate 2415.0
commentary: We have done a huge blow to their economy. 3 home system colonies gone, plus a fourth blockaded means we cut off almost half of their home system production (before applying maintenance).

The RP came in late, but we will buy Point-Defense 1 anyway (-20). Our maintenance is also very high, as we have fortified our homeworld quite well. (Just 9 CP is being spent towards offensive ships.) We take advantage of the recent paranoia reset, and place a bid of 8. The only way Minotaur can keep the initiative is to throw doubles.
Afterwards, we buy 10 Scouts (-60) at Andromeda. We will hold onto the rest of our resources.
The plasma storms have rolled 5,1 (in reading order). Both cosmic storms move.
{prodTable}{techTable}

Since Minotaur lost 3 home system colonies, it makes sense for them to do a concession check first before continuing. Granted, the aforementioned paranoia reset means the odds of them doing so are very low. Still, a 10 was rolled, which very barely passes this check.
Minotaur refuses to concede yet; their economic rolls are 1,3,8 (HS) / 3,10,10,10 (DS).

Their home systems are being beseiged, so they place a bid. 5,9 were rolled, and a net paranoia modifier of -2 causes them to place a bid of 3. Since we surpassed this bid, we take the initiative from them.
For fleet launch, a 10 was rolled. No launch takes place this time. Since there are no eligible deep space colonies this time, an FOB was instead placed in the home systems.

stages.heading: Stardate 2415.3
commentary: Since we have taken the initiative, we use it to give our offensive ships an extra move, and also try to eliminate one of their nebula miners. They rolled a 6 on the random encounter step (nothing).
Player Bombardments
Our lone Battlecruiser at Babbage (H8) can now bombard in earnest. A 1 was rolled (hit ≤6), damaging this colony. Our Bioweapons also made it to Anyon (F12), where they can glass it without fail.
The Battle for Sector H12
Once again, Minotaur saw the threat in the nebula to be the most grave, and sent their newest fleet there. After our Scout rolled a 9 (miss), their Fighters rolled a 1 and then some to mop it up.
The Battle for Terra

However, that would not be the only battle that takes place. A much bigger battle takes place at our homeworld once more. We have vastly reinforced it since it was last assaulted, and also upgraded anything that was outdated (used 3 CP this way). Since the assaulting fleet is already known, and that their carriers are at maximum fighters, we go straight into battle.
1. Round 1: As usual, we have the Fearless Race advantage to help us out, so we'll organize our rolls by Attack strength
• Our 1 Scout + 5 Battlecruisers + 11 Fighters have total Attack 7. We rolled 9/1,1,1,1,2,3,3,3,3,4,4,6,6,6,6,8 against their fighters (11 hits ≤4/5)
• Our Cruiser + Satellites have total Attack 6. We rolled 2,5 against the fighters (1 hit ≤4)
• Our 4 Carriers have total Attack 4. We rolled 4,7,7,10 against the fighters (0 hits ≤2)
• Their 6 Fighters rolled 2,2,2,7,7,9 against our fighters (6 hits ≤9)
• Their lone Cruiser rolled a 3 against our fighters (hit ≤6)
• Their 6 Carriers rolled 5,10,4,4,5,1 against our fighters (3 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Our Fearless Race bonus wore off, but some of our forces still get to shoot first
• Our Scout rolls a 3 against their fighters (hit ≤4)
• Our 5 Battlecruisers + 1 Fighter rolled 5,2,3,10,5,8 (4 hits ≤5)
• Our Satellites rolled a 7 against their last fighter (0 hits ≤4)
• Minotaur has already taken severe losses. They rolled a 55 for morale, which easily fails (≤91). They begin retreat procedures
• ... but before they can finish it, our Cruiser + 4 Carriers rolled 6,3,3,2/9 against their figher/carriers (1 hit ≤2/3)
• Only when their 6 Carriers finally get a chance to shoot do they also retreat. This would have also been the time they take their fighters with them... if we had not taken the last craft out

stages.heading: Stardate 2415.6
commentary: The economy damage continues. Before we conduct the random encounter step, we got a pair of black hole checks that need to be done. Our Scouts rolled 9/5, causing the ship closest to their homeworld to be sucked in.
On the random encounter step, a 1 was rolled. Nothing occurs yet again.
Player Bombardments
Our bombardment of Babbage (H8) continues. A 5 was rolled (hit ≤6), further damaging this colony. Our Bioweapons also made it to Essen (G11), where they can glass it without fail.
The Battle for Sector H12

As usual, Minotaur's defensive fleet intercepts the invader closest to their homeworld. But, before they can conduct a battle, they must also perform black hole checks. Their Scout rolls an 8. Their Carriers rolled 9,10. All of their forces get sucked in!!
The Battle for Terra
The extermination fleet still has decent strength, and has a valid pathway back home in order to buy a fighter restock. It can only afford a partial restock (only has CP for 5 fighters).
1. Round 1: We have 24 ships to their 9, easily securing the fleet size bonus
• Our 11 Scouts have the PD bonus, and we should spend it first. We rolled 2,5,7,3,3,1 against their fighters (5 hits ≤5)
• The remaining 5 Scouts rolled 4,1,9,7,2 against their carriers (3 hits ≤4)
• Our 5 Battlecruisers + 2 Fighters rolled 7,2,9,2,/4,5,5 against their carriers/cruiser (6 hits ≤7/6), wiping this fleet out!

stages.heading: Stardate 2415.9
commentary: This is probably the most advantageous state we have reached since they started launching their first fleet. Thanks to the fighter restock, they have no money left to support a third random encounter this phase.
Babbage (H8) receives one last bombardment roll before we conclude for the next economic phase. A 1 was rolled, finishing it off.

stages.heading: Stardate 2416.0
commentary: The blow against their economy widens. At Andromeda, we buy 3 Colony Ships (-24) + 6 Destroyers (-63).
The plasma storms have rolled 3,3 (in reading order). Both cosmic storms move once more.
{prodTable}{techTable}

Minotaur's losses have worsened considerably, so they conduct another concession check. A 45 was rolled. Since this paranoia check failed, no other steps the AP bot performs is meaningful, so we skip the rest of their phase.

stages.heading: Stardate 2416.0 (Conclusion)
commentary: And thus ends another AP Bot playthrough. After several stumbling blocks, we have achieved a drawn out victory. Bioweapons easily were our MVP for this playthrough, having managed to glass 7 of their colonies with relative ease.

It also did not help that the AP Bot system definitely has its share of limitations, both with the lack of expansion fleets heading our way, and with sending invaders <q>behind</q> their defensive fleets (although the latter is probably where the random encounter system comes into play). Not to mention we had an exceptionally lucky break when the entirety of their defensive fleet went down the black hole!

The use of Bioweapons against them is likely a good reason to use the prime directive. Being able to automatically glass colonies is huge! Yet, it could have just as easily conceded even if it took out our destroyers as soon as they could. Yes, their ships are very fast. Yet, we had scouts that we could use to slow them down (since they still have to stop all of their movement if they run into even a little bit of resistance).

Then there was the hilarious finding that AP Bots seem to be allergic to their own black holes. Even on a Massive size, roughly half of their home systems were cramped, making navigation difficult to perform.
